specification:
Type: chart **sim-id:** when-printing-arrived
**Library:** Chart.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** interpret
**Learning Objective:** The learner will interpret a chart of the years between Gutenberg's Bible and the first printing in ten scripts and places, answering at least 3 of 4 questions correctly. **Prerequisites:** Gutenberg, printing press, Hebrew press of 1493, İbrahim Müteferrika, delayed Arabic-script printing, millet system (defined in this chapter above). **Evidence of Mastery:** The learner answers four multiple-choice questions by reading the chart. An answer is correct when it matches the correct option in Feedback. Mastery is 3 of 4 correct on the first attempt. **Misconceptions:** (1) There were no printing presses in Istanbul before 1727. (2) Arabic script could not be printed at all before the 18th century. (3) The delay applied to everyone in the Ottoman Empire, rather than to printing in Arabic script for Muslim readers. (4) The ban of 1485 is established fact. **Instructional Rationale:** A chart of years-after-Gutenberg makes the length of each gap visible and lets the learner compare communities in the same city. Questions that require reading specific bars expose the misconception that Istanbul had no presses, which the chapter's prose alone may not dislodge. **Content:** A horizontal bar chart. Each bar is the number of years from 1455 (Gutenberg's Bible) to the first printing named. Bars are grouped as "Western Europe" or "Ottoman Empire". Clicking or hovering a bar shows its infobox text. | # | Bar label | Group | First printing | Years after 1455 | Infobox text | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Latin, Mainz | Western Europe | about 1455 | 0 | Gutenberg's 42-line Bible, about 180 copies. | | 2 | Latin, Venice | Western Europe | 1469 | 14 | The first press in Venice, soon the printing capital of Europe. | | 3 | Hebrew, Italy | Western Europe | 1475 | 20 | The first dated Hebrew books, printed in southern and northern Italy. | | 4 | Greek, Milan | Western Europe | 1476 | 21 | The first book printed entirely in Greek, a grammar. | | 5 | Hebrew, Istanbul | Ottoman Empire | 1493 | 38 | The ibn Nahmias brothers, Sephardic refugees, print a code of Jewish law; some scholars date it about ten years later. | | 6 | Arabic script, Italy | Western Europe | 1514 | 59 | A Christian prayer book in Arabic printed in Italy for Arabic-speaking Christians. | | 7 | Armenian, Istanbul | Ottoman Empire | 1567 | 112 | The first Armenian press in the Ottoman capital. | | 8 | Greek, Istanbul | Ottoman Empire | 1627 | 172 | A Greek press set up with the support of the Ecumenical Patriarch. | | 9 | Arabic script, Aleppo | Ottoman Empire | 1706 | 251 | An Arabic press for Christian books in Ottoman Syria. | | 10 | Ottoman Turkish (Arabic script), Istanbul | Ottoman Empire | 1729 | 274 | İbrahim Müteferrika's first book, a dictionary, 1,000 copies. | The chart title is "Years from Gutenberg's Bible to the first printing", and the axis is labeled "Years after 1455". **Provenance:** Bars 1, 5, 7, 8 and 10 come from this chapter's sections "Gutenberg", "The Hebrew Press of 1493" and "İbrahim Müteferrika". Bars 2, 3, 4, 6 and 9 come from the Wikipedia articles "Global spread of the printing press", "Hebrew printing" (Italy, 1475), "Constantine Lascaris" (Milan, 1476), "Kitab Salat al-Sawai" (1514) and "Athanasius III Dabbas" (Aleppo, 1706). Years after 1455 are computed as the first-printing year minus 1455. **Rules:** Bars are ordered by year, earliest at the top. Years after 1455 = first-printing year − 1455. All ten bars are shown from the start. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner reads the chart title and axis. 2. The learner opens the infobox for several bars. 3. The learner answers the four questions below. 4. The learner should notice that every Ottoman bar before 1729 belongs to a non-Muslim community or to Christians printing Arabic. **Feedback:** Four multiple-choice questions, in this order, one attempt each: 1. "Which community printed first in Istanbul?" Options: (a) Jewish [correct]; (b) Greek; (c) Muslim Ottoman. Correct: "Yes: the ibn Nahmias brothers, about 1493." Incorrect: "Look at bar 5." 2. "About how many years after Gutenberg's Bible did the first Ottoman Turkish book in Arabic script appear?" Options: (a) about 40; (b) about 170; (c) about 275 [correct]. Correct: "Right: 1729, about 274 years after 1455." Incorrect: "Look at bar 10." 3. "Which statement fits the chart?" Options: (a) Istanbul had no printing presses before 1727; (b) Presses ran in Istanbul for more than two centuries before Arabic-script printing for Muslim readers began [correct]; (c) Arabic script was first printed in Istanbul. Correct: "Yes: Jewish, Armenian and Greek presses came first." Incorrect: "Look at bars 5, 7 and 8." 4. "What does bar 6 show about the delay?" Options: (a) Arabic script could be printed by 1514, so the delay was not only technical [correct]; (b) Italy banned Arabic printing; (c) Arabic printing began in Aleppo. Correct: "Right: the technology existed; the reasons for waiting were also cultural, economic and political." Incorrect: "Compare bar 6 with bar 10." At the end: 3 or 4 correct shows "You can read the gap and explain what it does and doesn't mean."; fewer shows "Open the Ottoman bars again and check who did the printing." **Starting State:** The full chart with all ten bars, and the question "Who printed first in Istanbul?" **Chapter Anchors:** Gutenberg's Bible about 1455, about 180 copies; Hebrew press dated 1493 (possibly about ten years later); Armenian press in Istanbul 1567; Greek press in Istanbul 1627; Müteferrika's decree 1727 and first book 1729, 1,000 copies; gap of about 275 years; ten bars; mastery 3 of 4.
